abstracts.abstract: Includes certain violations involving physical, psychological, or emotional harm to a child as qualifying offenses for the purpose of imposing bail.

bill.title: Includes certain violations involving children as qualifying offenses for the purpose of imposing bail

posted_text:
💰 NY A11713 — Could You Be Released on Own Recognizance in a Crime Against a Child

This bill could change how a judge decides whether to release someone accused of harming a child.

Currently, prosecutors have to show a clear reason why a defendant committed a crime and any related crimes.

This bill would allow a judge to consider whether the crime – like theft or assault – was minor and not part of a larger criminal plan, potentially leading to release on own recognizance or with non-monetary conditions.

Specifically, the bill expands the types of crimes considered, including criminal possession of a firearm and causing physical, psychological, or emotional harm to a child under 18.

It also affects cases where a defendant is released on recognizance or a desk appearance ticket for a separate, related offense.

Sept. 16, 2026: Referred to Codes.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A11713
